title: Can the main method be overloaded?
shortTitle: Can the main method be overloaded?
keyPoints: Yes, you can overload main – you can have main(int[]), main(String), main() alongside main(String[])
The JVM always calls public static void main(String[] args) as the entry point
Overloaded versions are just regular static methods – you can call them from the real main
Overloading main is legal but confusing – avoid it in production code
Understanding this concept is essential for Java interviews at senior level

s1_definition.oneliner: Yes, main can be overloaded with different parameter types. But the JVM always calls the String[] version as the entry point. The others are just regular methods.
s1_definition.profdef:
Overloading means having multiple methods with the same name but different parameters:

- **Legal.** You can define `main(String[] args)`, `main(int count)`, `main()`, and `main(String single)` in the same class.
- **Entry point is fixed.** The JVM always looks for `public static void main(String[] args)`. The overloaded versions are never called by the JVM directly.
- **Just regular methods.** The overloaded mains can be called from the real main or from other code.
s1_definition.analogy: The bank branch has one official front door (the String[] version). You can build other doors (overloaded versions), but the public always enters through the official one. Staff can use the other doors internally.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Class has: main(String[]), main(int), main(String)
    │
    ▼
  JVM looks for: public static void main(String[] args)
    │
    ├─ Found → calls it (entry point)
    │    │
    │    └─ main(String[]) can call main(int), main(String) internally
    │
    └─ Not found → "Main method not found" (ignores overloads)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Yes, you can overload the main method with different parameter types. The class can have main(String[]), main(int), main(), and main(String single) all at once. But the JVM always calls the String[] version as the entry point. The overloaded versions are just regular static methods that you can call from the real main or from other code.

If the String[] version is missing, the JVM reports "Main method not found" even if other overloads exist. It does not search for alternatives.

One sentence to remember: main can be overloaded, but only the String[] version is the JVM entry point – the others are just regular methods.
